subject: CDBG Action Plan
overview: The Committee of the Whole met to review applicant proposals and initial allocation recommendations for the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Year 49 Action Plan public service funds. The committee voted to receive the presentations and place the matter on file ahead of a formal public hearing scheduled for May.

items.title: CDBG Action Plan Year 49 Overview
items.summary: Director of Planning, Development and Sustainability Alicia Hunt outlined the Year 49 CDBG public service allocation process, noting request totals exceeded available funding and outlining where alternate sources like ARPA and CDBG-CV were recommended.

items.title: Council on Aging Funding Request
items.summary: Director Pam Kelly presented a $30,000 request to fund minor home repairs, day-trip transportation discounts, social work hours, volunteer coordination, and a Mystic Valley Elder Services match.

items.title: Medford Public Schools Before and After School Programs
items.summary: Megan Fidler-Carey requested CDBG support to provide tuition assistance and outreach for low- and moderate-income students enrolled in after-school programs.

items.title: West Medford Community Center Elder Services
items.summary: Lisa Crossman requested $21,000 to fund the elder services director position and provide social, cultural, and day-trip programming for local seniors.

items.title: Megan Transport Grocery Shuttle Proposal and Senior Transit
items.summary: Neema Jama outlined a $56,000 proposal for a grocery shuttle pilot connecting Medford Housing Authority properties with affordable supermarkets, prompting council discussion on regional transportation costs and a potential municipal transit task force.

items.title: Housing Families Homelessness Prevention and Legal Services
items.summary: Heather Van Orman requested CDBG funds to deliver free legal defense, homelessness prevention case management, and rental support to Medford households at risk of eviction.

items.title: Mystic Valley YMCA Mystic Community Market
items.summary: Lindsay Smyth discussed operating needs and relocation planning for the Mystic Community Market, which serves approximately 5,000 food-insecure Medford residents annually.

items.title: SCM Transportation Demand-Response Services
items.summary: Executive Director John Keegan described SCM's door-to-door transportation services for medical visits and grocery shopping for low-income seniors.

items.title: Immigrant Learning Center English and Literacy Programs
items.summary: Mark Correa requested continued support for the Immigrant Learning Center's English classes, civics education, and citizenship programs for immigrants and refugees.

items.title: Evangelical Church of Holiness Citizenship Program
items.summary: Director Hunt summarized a funding recommendation to support the Evangelical Church of Holiness's pathway to citizenship program serving the local Haitian community.

items.title: The Community Family Alzheimer's Day Care
items.summary: Ann Marchetta requested CDBG funding to bridge adult day healthcare costs for families caring for individuals with Alzheimer's who are pending Medicaid eligibility.

items.title: Communitas Recreational Services
items.summary: Jason Maria presented an application for ARPA funding to restart swim, track, and family support programs for individuals with developmental disabilities.

items.title: Bread of Life Grocery Delivery
items.summary: Gabriella Stelmak requested support to provide home grocery deliveries to homebound Medford seniors and disabled residents.

items.title: Action for Boston Community Development (ABCD) Housing Services
items.summary: Representatives from ABCD presented a request for rental assistance and stabilization programs, confirming that city funding is dedicated exclusively to Medford residents.

items.title: Adjournment
items.summary: The council voted to receive and place the matter on file ahead of a formal public hearing on the complete CDBG plan in May.
